svg.title: Allocate Startup Capital without Mistaking It for Annual Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-four-bucket-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate Startup Capital without Mistaking It for Annual Profit; subtitle: Four buckets sum to a $45,000 reference launch budget.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values depict the $45,000 reference budget. Stage details also specify allocations for the canonical $15,000 minimum and $120,000 maximum: each column sums exactly to its total. These are illustrative cash allocations, not accounting capitalization instructions or additional annual costs.; caption: Reference allocation is $18,000 + $12,000 + $9,000 + $6,000 = $45,000. A startup budget does not fund the entire canonical 6–24-month path to the first deal; calculate continuing funding separately.; stages: label: Original content and evidence; value: $18,000 reference allocation; 40% of launch cash; numeric value: 18000.0; detail: Allocate $6,000 at the minimum, $18,000 at reference, or $48,000 at maximum. Fund original testing, commissioned writing, editing, and documented media licenses.; label: Technical publishing foundation; value: $12,000 reference allocation; 26.67% of launch cash; numeric value: 12000.0; detail: Allocate $4,000 at the minimum, $12,000 at reference, or $32,000 at maximum. Fund templates, hosting setup, backups, access controls, and initial crawl remediation.; label: Measurement and commercial setup; value: $9,000 reference allocation; 20% of launch cash; numeric value: 9000.0; detail: Allocate $3,000 at the minimum, $9,000 at reference, or $24,000 at maximum. Fund attribution setup, reporting connectors, partner materials, and contributor agreement preparation.; label: Unspent working reserve; value: $6,000 reference allocation; 13.33% of launch cash; numeric value: 6000.0; detail: Allocate $2,000 at the minimum, $6,000 at reference, or $16,000 at maximum. The reference reserve covers two months at $3,000 monthly opex or 0.3 months at $20,000; reserve cash is not an incurred expense.
